  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.

      properties:
        type:
          title: Type

          title: Timestamp

          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors

          type: array

      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create the value is
            normalized to E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped;
            a leading '+' and country code are kept when present, otherwise
            country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped
            from the national digits. The stored value must have 8 to 15 digits
            after the '+' (e.g. '0412 345 678' is stored as '+61412345678').
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The optional email address of the pet owner. When present it must be
            a syntactically valid address; it is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: >-
            The optional 4-digit postcode of the pet owner. When present it must be
            valid for the owner's city per a fixed table keyed by the city's region
            ('Sydney' -> NSW 2000-2099, 'Melbourne' -> VIC 3000-3099, 'Brisbane' ->
            QLD 4000-4099). A city with no known region accepts any 4-digit postcode.
            A postcode that is malformed or out of range for the city's region is
            rejected with a 400. Stored and returned when given.
          type: string
          pattern: "^[0-9]{4}$"
          example: '2000'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            When omitted on create it defaults to the server's current date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date
          description: >-
            The optional date of birth of the pet owner, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD'
            format. When present it is used to derive the owner's 'ageBand'.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Optional create-time directive. When true, the owner is permitted to
            share a household with an existing owner, so the create request is not
            rejected as a household duplicate even when another owner has the same
            last name and address (compared case-insensitively with collapsed
            whitespace).
          type: boolean
          example: true
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            locality:
              title: Locality
              description: >-
                The owner's locality (region), derived by preferring the postcode: a 4-digit
                postcode within a known region's range ('NSW' 2000-2099, 'VIC' 3000-3099,
                'QLD' 4000-4099) yields that region. When the postcode is absent or in no known
                range, it falls back to a fixed city-to-region table ('Sydney' -> 'NSW',
                'Melbourne' -> 'VIC', 'Brisbane' -> 'QLD'). A city not in the table with no
                region-bearing postcode derives the locality 'UNKNOWN'.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                The owner's customer code, formatted '<LAST3>-<NNNN>' where LAST3 is the
                upper-cased first three letters of lastName and NNNN is a global 4-digit
                zero-padded sequence equal to one more than the number of owners at the
                time the owner was created.
              type: string
              example: 'SMI-0007'
              readOnly: true
            checkDigit:
              title: Check digit
              description: >-
                A single Luhn check digit (0-9) computed over the digits contained in the
                customerCode.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              maximum: 9
              example: 4
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: >-
                The owner's membership number, formatted '<customerCode>-M<YY>' where
                YY is the last two digits of the registrationDate year.
              type: string
              example: 'SMI-0007-M26'
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: >-
                A stable identifier shared by every owner in the same household - those with
                the same last name and address, compared case-insensitively with collapsed
                whitespace. Owners who opt in with 'sharesHousehold' to join an existing
                household receive that household's identifier.
              type: string
              example: 'a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9012345678901234567890abcdef123456'
              readOnly: true
            identityKey:
              title: Identity key
              description: >-
                The owner's derived duplicate-detection key, formed by joining the normalized
                telephone, the email (or an empty string when absent) and the householdId with
                '|' separators (normalizedTelephone + '|' + email + '|' + householdId). A create
                is rejected as a duplicate only when this whole key equals that of an existing
                owner.
              type: string
              example: '+61412345678|george.franklin@example.com|a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9012345678901234567890abcdef123456'
              readOnly: true
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: >-
                The number of existing owners, at the time this owner was created, sharing the
                same first name and last name, compared case-insensitively.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            membershipLevel:
              title: Membership level
              description: >-
                The owner's numeric membership level, computed on creation. Starts at 1;
                add 1 when an email is present; add 1 when namesakeCount is 0; capped at 3.
                (Level 4 is reserved for tenure.)
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 1
              maximum: 4
              example: 3
              readOnly: true
            bulkSignupWarning:
              title: Bulk signup warning
              description: >-
                True when more than 80 owners had already been created for this owner's
                registration date at the time this owner was created, otherwise false.
              type: boolean
              example: false
              readOnly: true
            contactPreference:
              title: Contact preference
              description: >-
                The owner's preferred contact channel, derived from the presence of an
                email: 'EMAIL' when an email is present, otherwise 'PHONE'.
              type: string
              enum:
                - EMAIL
                - PHONE
              example: 'EMAIL'
              readOnly: true
            ageBand:
              title: Age band
              description: >-
                The owner's age band, derived from 'birthDate' measured against the
                owner's 'registrationDate': 'MINOR' when under 18, 'ADULT' from 18 to
                64, and 'SENIOR' at 65 or older. Absent when no 'birthDate' is given.
              type: string
              enum:
                - MINOR
                - ADULT
                - SENIOR
              example: 'ADULT'
              readOnly: true
            pets:
              title: Pets
              description: The pets owned by this individual including any booked vet visits.
              type: array
              items:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
              readOnly: true
          required:
            - pets

## Summary

I implemented the soft-duplicate ("possible duplicate") detection for owner creation. When a new owner is not a hard duplicate but shares an existing owner's `lastName` and `postcode` with a different telephone, it is still created and now reports `possibleDuplicate: true` with `possibleDuplicateOf` set to the matching owner's id; otherwise `possibleDuplicate: false`.

Changes:

- **`openapi.yml`** — added two read-only fields to the `Owner` schema: `possibleDuplicate` (boolean) and `possibleDuplicateOf` (int32). These generate the corresponding `OwnerDto` accessors, and MapStruct auto-maps them from the `Owner` entity by name.
- **`Owner.java`** — added persisted `possibleDuplicate` (`Boolean`) and `possibleDuplicateOf` (`Integer`) columns with getters/setters, so the values computed at create time survive to the `GET` read-back.
- **`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`** — after the hard-duplicate identity check passes, it computes the soft-match via a new `findPossibleDuplicate(owner)` helper and stores the result on the owner before saving.
- **`findPossibleDuplicate`** — returns the oldest existing owner (lowest id) that matches `lastName` (case-insensitively) and `postcode` while carrying a *different* normalized telephone; returns `null` when the owner has no postcode or no such match. The controller sets `possibleDuplicate` from whether that id is non-null.
- **Schema files** (`hsqldb`, `h2`, `mysql`, `postgres`) — added `possible_duplicate` and `possible_duplicate_of` columns to the `owners` table so the entity maps cleanly across all supported databases (tests run on hsqldb).

The logic sits after `rejectDuplicateIdentity`, so it only ever flags owners that were accepted (i.e., genuinely not hard duplicates), matching the spec's "not a hard duplicate but shares…" wording.
